extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, theology, and natural philosophy (educated laymen or scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative principles and criticisms about what counts as genuine philosophy, natural philosophy, and legitimate religious/political practice as presented in an early-modern political-philosophical treatise. Includes criteria for explanatory adequacy, sources of knowledge, and proper measures for moral and political judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: By Philosophy is understood 'the Knowledge acquired by Reasoning, from the Manner of the Generation of any thing, to the Properties; or from the Properties, to some possible Way of Generation of the same; to the end to bee able to produce, as far as matter, and humane force permit, such Effects, as humane life requireth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy is knowledge produced by reasoning that links causes (manner of generation) to properties and vice versa, with the practical aim of producing effects useful for human life. Examples: geometry (from construction to properties and back), astronomy (from movements to causes and to timekeeping). Emphasize demonstrative, cause-to-effect or effect-to-cause reasoning rather than mere description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence not part of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prudence (original knowledge called Experience) is not to be accounted part of Philosophy because it is not attained by Reasoning but is a memory of successions of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between prudence/experience (particular, contingent, memory-based know-how) and philosophical knowledge (general, eternal, derived by reasoning). Do not treat empirically acquired habits or contingent experience as philosophical demonstrations; recognize their practical utility but not their status as philosophical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supernatural revelation is not philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor to that which any man knows by supernaturall Revelation; because it is not acquired by Reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify knowledge learned from revelation as distinct from philosophical knowledge; revelation may be authoritative for faith but does not belong to philosophy proper because it isn't derived by reasoning from causes/effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning taken on authority is not philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor that which is gotten by Reasoning from the Authority of Books; because it is not by Reasoning from the Cause to the Effect, nor from the Effect to the Cause; and is not Knowledge, but Faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject appeals to authority as substitutes for causal reasoning. If a claim is accepted merely on an author's authority rather than derived by cause/effect reasoning, treat it as faith or received opinion, not philosophical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure and commonwealth are prerequisites for philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Leasure is the mother of Philosophy; and Common-wealth, the mother of Peace, and Leasure: Where first were great and flourishing Cities, there was first the study of Philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize social and material conditions (peace, leisure, urban institutions) as necessary enabling conditions for the systematic study and transmission of philosophical knowledge. Evaluate claims about origins of sciences with attention to socio-political context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities often teach 'Aristotelity' not true philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: And for the study of Philosophy it hath no otherwise place, then as a handmaid to the Romane Religion: And since the Authority of Aristotle is onely current there, that study is not properly Philosophy, (the nature whereof dependeth not on Authors,) but Aristotelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be critical of institutionalized teaching that substitutes deference to an authoritative author (Aristotle) for genuine philosophical reasoning. Evaluate curricula for whether they foster independent causal reasoning or merely transmit received doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject belief in separated abstract essences (abstracted substantial forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: They teach there be in the world certaine Essences separated from Bodies, which they call Abstract Essences, and Substantiall Formes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat metaphysical reification of 'abstract essences' as suspect. Challenge claims that posit incorporeal, spatially indeterminate 'essences' separate from bodies; expose the practical and conceptual absurdities (e.g., a soul 'all of it' in every part of the body). Prefer accounts that avoid postulating occult, non-spatial entities to ground ordinary phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid meaningless scholastic distinctions (definitive vs. circumscriptive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because they hold them Incorporeall, without all dimension of Quantity... they are driven to uphold their credit with a distinction, that they are not indeed any where Circumscriptive, but Definitive: Which Terms being meer Words, and in this occasion insignificant, passe onely in Latine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of technical distinctions that obscure rather than clarify. Flag jargon that substitutes verbal sleight-of-hand for genuine explanatory content. Demand that terms have clear empirical or logical roles rather than serving to hide contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal explanations must not be circular or tautological
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schools will tell you... the bodies that sink downwards, are Heavy; and that this Heavinesse is it that causes them to descend: But if you ask what they mean by Heavinesse, they will define it to bee an endeavour to goe to the center of the Earth... so that the cause why things sink downward, is an Endeavour to be below: which is as much as to say, that bodies descend, or ascend, because they doe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explanatory accounts that do explanatory work (identify mechanisms, relations) rather than renaming the phenomenon as its cause. Avoid definitions that amount to restating the observed effect as its cause; prefer mechanistic, mathematical, or testable explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not invoke occult or ignorance-disguised causes
rubrics_metrics.description: In many occasions they put for cause of Naturall events, their own Ignorance, but disguised in other words: As when they say, Fortune is the cause of things contingent... Occult Qualities... Sympathy, Antipathy, Antiperistasis, Specificall Qualities...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat appeals to 'occult qualities', 'sympathy', 'fortune', etc., as placeholders for ignorance, not genuine explanations. Insist that purported causes be explicable or at least constrained by observable relations; label unexplained labels as anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not derive moral good from private appetite in commonwealths
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle, and other Heathen Philosophers define Good, and Evill, by the Appetite of men... But in a Common-wealth this measure is false: Not the Appetite of Private men, but the Law, which is the Will and Appetite of the State is the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In political and civil philosophy, use the law (the will/appetite of the state) as the measure of public good and evil rather than individual private appetites. Evaluate moral-political claims by reference to the legal/political order that secures common peace and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question claims that lawful marriage is unchastity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also Vain and false Philosophy, to say the work of Marriage is repugnant to Chastity, or Continence, and by consequence to make them Morall Vices; as they doe, that pretend Chastity, and Continence, for the ground of denying Marriage to the Clergy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize moral doctrines that denounce ordinary social institutions (marriage) without sufficient philosophical or political justification. Consider whether such doctrines serve clerical or political interests rather than genuine moral truth; seek historically grounded explanations (e.g., institutional motives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate all non-popular governments with tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: From Aristotles Civill Philosophy, they have learned, to call all manner of Common-wealths but the Popular... All Kings they called Tyrants... A Tyrant originally signified no more simply, but a Monarch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rhetorical conflation of monarchy, aristocracy, or oligarchy with 'tyranny' solely on basis of non-popularity. Evaluate regimes by their effects (peace, order, stability) rather than by nominal labels that carry partisan connotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws require men and force to be effective (men and arms, not words, give laws power)
rubrics_metrics.description: it is Men, and Arms, not Words, and Promises, that make the Force and Power of the Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In political theory, recognize that abstract laws require human agents and enforcement to secure obedience. Critique doctrines that imagine laws alone (without executive force or authority) will govern effectively; assess institutions for their capacity to enforce and realize legal rules.
